q: 你想喝茶___咖啡？
zh: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？
py: nǐ xiǎng hē chá hái shì kā fēi
en: Do you want tea or coffee?
why: You are asking the listener to pick one, so the "or" is 还是. 或者 only lists possibilities in statements, and 和 means "and", which makes no question.

q: 医生，我是吃药___打针？
zh: 医生，我是吃药还是打针？
py: yī shēng wǒ shì chī yào hái shì dǎ zhēn
en: Doctor, should I take medicine or get an injection?
why: The patient wants the doctor to choose between two treatments, a direct question, so 还是. 或者 cannot ask "which one?".

q: 你今天在公司___在家？
zh: 你今天在公司还是在家？
py: nǐ jīn tiān zài gōng sī hái shì zài jiā
en: Are you at the office or at home today?
why: A question that wants one answer between two places takes 还是. 和 would join the two as "and" and 或者 does not ask for a pick.

q: 他是医生___护士？
zh: 他是医生还是护士？
py: tā shì yī shēng hái shì hù shì
en: Is he a doctor or a nurse?
why: Only one of the two can be true and the speaker wants to know which, so 还是. 或者 belongs in statements that list possibilities.

q: 会议是上午开___下午开？
zh: 会议是上午开还是下午开？
py: huì yì shì shàng wǔ kāi hái shì xià wǔ kāi
en: Is the meeting in the morning or in the afternoon?
why: The speaker asks which of two times, so the options are linked by 还是. 还有 means "and also" and 或者 would not ask for a choice.

q: 这份文件是你写的___小王写的？
zh: 这份文件是你写的还是小王写的？
py: zhè fèn wén jiàn shì nǐ xiě de hái shì xiǎo wáng xiě de
en: Did you write this document, or did Xiao Wang?
why: Asking who wrote it, with two candidates, is a choice question and takes 还是. 或者 only lists options in a statement.

q: 是你的头疼___肚子疼？
zh: 是你的头疼还是肚子疼？
py: shì nǐ de tóu téng hái shì dù zi téng
en: Is it your head or your stomach that hurts?
why: The doctor needs one of the two answers, so 还是. 或者 cannot carry the question "which?", and 和 would say both hurt.

q: 你打算发邮件通知他___打电话通知他？
zh: 你打算发邮件通知他还是打电话通知他？
py: nǐ dǎ suàn fā yóu jiàn tōng zhī tā hái shì dǎ diàn huà tōng zhī tā
en: Are you going to notify him by email or by phone?
why: Two ways of doing it and the listener must say which: 还是. 或者 would only list ways in a statement, and 还有 adds a further item.

q: 你要喝冷水___热水？
zh: 你要喝冷水还是热水？
py: nǐ yào hē lěng shuǐ hái shì rè shuǐ
en: Would you like cold water or hot water?
why: Offering a choice and waiting for the listener to pick one is exactly where 还是 is used. 和 would mean both cold and hot water.

q: 你觉得这个问题应该先问经理___先问同事？
zh: 你觉得这个问题应该先问经理还是先问同事？
py: nǐ jué de zhè ge wèn tí yīng gāi xiān wèn jīng lǐ hái shì xiān wèn tóng shì
en: Do you think I should ask the manager first or ask a colleague first?
why: The speaker wants advice on which of two first steps, a direct choice question, so 还是. 或者 would not ask for a pick.

q: 你来我的办公室___我去你的办公室？
zh: 你来我的办公室还是我去你的办公室？
py: nǐ lái wǒ de bàn gōng shì hái shì wǒ qù nǐ de bàn gōng shì
en: Will you come to my office, or shall I go to yours?
why: Two whole clauses with different subjects are offered as a choice: 还是 goes before the second clause. 或者 does not fit a question.

q: 你的感冒是昨天开始的___前天开始的？
zh: 你的感冒是昨天开始的还是前天开始的？
py: nǐ de gǎn mào shì zuó tiān kāi shǐ de hái shì qián tiān kāi shǐ de
en: Did your cold start yesterday or the day before?
why: The doctor asks which day it started. A question wanting one of two answers takes 还是, not 或者.

q: 你们今天开会___明天开会？
zh: 你们今天开会还是明天开会？
py: nǐ men jīn tiān kāi huì hái shì míng tiān kāi huì
en: Are you having the meeting today or tomorrow?
why: Asking which day the meeting is on is a choice question, so 还是. 和 would make "today and tomorrow", and 或者 asks nothing.

q: 复印机是没纸了___没电了？
zh: 复印机是没纸了还是没电了？
py: fù yìn jī shì méi zhǐ le hái shì méi diàn le
en: Is the copier out of paper or out of power?
why: The speaker wants to know which of two causes it is, so 还是. 也是 means "also is" and 或者 cannot ask "which?".

q: 你想吃苹果还是香蕉___？
zh: 你想吃苹果还是香蕉？
py: nǐ xiǎng chī píng guǒ hái shì xiāng jiāo
en: Do you want an apple or a banana?
why: A 还是 question is already a complete question; leave the end bare. 吗 asks for yes or no, and "apple or banana" cannot be answered with yes or no.

q: 他是经理还是同事___？
zh: 他是经理还是同事？
py: tā shì jīng lǐ hái shì tóng shì
en: Is he the manager or a colleague?
why: 还是 already makes the sentence a question, so 吗 is never added. The answer is "manager" or "colleague", not yes or no.

q: 你坐地铁还是打车___？
zh: 你坐地铁还是打车呢？
py: nǐ zuò dì tiě hái shì dǎ chē ne
en: Are you taking the subway or a taxi?
why: A 还是 question can end bare or with the soft 呢 but never with 吗. 吗 expects a yes or no answer, which is impossible here.

q: 我们在家开会还是去公司开会___？
zh: 我们在家开会还是去公司开会呢？
py: wǒ men zài jiā kāi huì hái shì qù gōng sī kāi huì ne
en: Shall we hold the meeting at home or go to the office for it?
why: With 还是 the sentence-final particle can only be 呢 (or nothing). 吗 clashes because the answer is one of the options.

q: 你的咳嗽是白天重还是晚上重___？
zh: 你的咳嗽是白天重还是晚上重？
py: nǐ de ké sòu shì bái tiān zhòng hái shì wǎn shàng zhòng
en: Is your cough worse in the daytime or at night?
why: The question offers two times and wants one, so no 吗. Adding 吗 would turn it into a yes/no question that contradicts the choice.

q: 你周六有空还是周日有空___？
zh: 你周六有空还是周日有空？
py: nǐ zhōu liù yǒu kòng hái shì zhōu rì yǒu kòng
en: Are you free on Saturday or on Sunday?
why: 还是 asks which day, so the sentence ends bare. 吗 would ask for yes or no, which cannot answer "Saturday or Sunday?".

q: 你打算在办公室吃午饭还是出去吃___？
zh: 你打算在办公室吃午饭还是出去吃呢？
py: nǐ dǎ suàn zài bàn gōng shì chī wǔ fàn hái shì chū qù chī ne
en: Are you planning to eat lunch at the office or go out for it?
why: A choice question ends bare or with 呢, never 吗. The listener answers with one of the two plans, not with yes or no.

q: 你喝水还是喝果汁___？
zh: 你喝水还是喝果汁？
py: nǐ hē shuǐ hái shì hē guǒ zhī
en: Will you have water or juice?
why: 还是 already marks this as a choice question, so nothing follows. 吗 would add a yes/no question to a sentence that cannot be answered yes or no.

q: 你是先去医院检查还是先回家休息___？
zh: 你是先去医院检查还是先回家休息？
py: nǐ shì xiān qù yī yuàn jiǎn chá hái shì xiān huí jiā xiū xī
en: Will you go to the hospital for a check-up first, or go home to rest first?
why: Two plans, one answer wanted: 还是 and nothing at the end. 吗 would cancel the choice by asking for yes or no.

q: 你周六___周日有空吗？
zh: 你周六或者周日有空吗？
py: nǐ zhōu liù huò zhě zhōu rì yǒu kòng ma
en: Are you free on Saturday or Sunday?
why: Here 吗 makes it a yes/no question ("free on either day?"), so the "or" inside is 或者. 还是 cannot be used together with 吗.

q: 我不知道他去___不去。
zh: 我不知道他去还是不去。
py: wǒ bù zhī dào tā qù hái shì bù qù
en: I don't know whether he is going or not.
why: After 不知道 the choice is still open, so 还是 joins 去 and 不去 even though the sentence ends with a full stop. 或者 would state both as possible.

q: 我不知道她是经理___同事。
zh: 我不知道她是经理还是同事。
py: wǒ bù zhī dào tā shì jīng lǐ hái shì tóng shì
en: I don't know whether she is the manager or a colleague.
why: The speaker does not know which, so the choice is still an open question inside the statement. That takes 还是, not 或者.

q: 我还没决定明天去开会___在家工作。
zh: 我还没决定明天去开会还是在家工作。
py: wǒ hái méi jué dìng míng tiān qù kāi huì hái shì zài jiā gōng zuò
en: I haven't decided whether to go to the meeting tomorrow or work from home.
why: 没决定 means the choice is open, so 还是. 或者 would list two settled possibilities.

q: 医生问我头疼是早上疼___晚上疼。
zh: 医生问我头疼是早上疼还是晚上疼。
py: yī shēng wèn wǒ tóu téng shì zǎo shàng téng hái shì wǎn shàng téng
en: The doctor asked me whether my headache is in the morning or in the evening.
why: 问 reports a question, and the inner clause still asks "which?". Reported choice questions keep 还是.

q: 请告诉我你想周一开会___周二开会。
zh: 请告诉我你想周一开会还是周二开会。
py: qǐng gào su wǒ nǐ xiǎng zhōu yī kāi huì hái shì zhōu èr kāi huì
en: Please tell me whether you want the meeting on Monday or on Tuesday.
why: 告诉我 hands the choice to the listener to decide, so the clause is an open question and takes 还是. 和 would mean both days.

q: 我想知道这个药是饭前吃___饭后吃。
zh: 我想知道这个药是饭前吃还是饭后吃。
py: wǒ xiǎng zhī dào zhè ge yào shì fàn qián chī hái shì fàn hòu chī
en: I want to know whether this medicine is taken before or after meals.
why: 想知道 introduces an unanswered question, so the choice is joined by 还是. 或者 would present both as acceptable.

q: 我不确定经理是想自己参加会议___让我们去。
zh: 我不确定经理是想自己参加会议还是让我们去。
py: wǒ bù què dìng jīng lǐ shì xiǎng zì jǐ cān jiā huì yì hái shì ràng wǒ men qù
en: I'm not sure whether the manager wants to attend the meeting himself or have us go.
why: 不确定 means the choice is unresolved, which is the job of 还是. 或者 would say that either is the plan.

q: 他没告诉我们他是坐飞机来___坐火车来。
zh: 他没告诉我们他是坐飞机来还是坐火车来。
py: tā méi gào su wǒ men tā shì zuò fēi jī lái hái shì zuò huǒ chē lái
en: He didn't tell us whether he is coming by plane or by train.
why: 没告诉 leaves the answer unknown, so the inner clause is an open question and takes 还是. 或者 would make both modes part of the plan.

q: 你猜他是病了___累了？
zh: 你猜他是病了还是累了？
py: nǐ cāi tā shì bìng le hái shì lèi le
en: Do you guess he is sick or just tired?
why: 猜 asks the listener to pick one of two explanations, so the choice is open. 还是 is needed; 或者 gives no choice.

q: 老板问我们是现在开会___吃完饭再开会。
zh: 老板问我们是现在开会还是吃完饭再开会。
py: lǎo bǎn wèn wǒ men shì xiàn zài kāi huì hái shì chī wán fàn zài kāi huì
en: The boss asked whether we should meet now or after we have eaten.
why: The boss is waiting for the team to choose between two times, so the reported question takes 还是. 或者 would lay out both as fine.

q: 我周末想在家看书___看电影。
zh: 我周末想在家看书或者看电影。
py: wǒ zhōu mò xiǎng zài jiā kàn shū huò zhě kàn diàn yǐng
en: This weekend I'd like to read or watch a film at home.
why: The speaker is just stating two things they might do; nobody is asked to choose. Statements list alternatives with 或者.

q: 我午饭常常吃面条___米饭。
zh: 我午饭常常吃面条或者米饭。
py: wǒ wǔ fàn cháng cháng chī miàn tiáo huò zhě mǐ fàn
en: For lunch I often eat noodles or rice.
why: A plain statement about habits lists what happens; there is no question to pick from, so 或者. 还是 would sound like an open question.

q: 你可以给经理发邮件___打电话。
zh: 你可以给经理发邮件或者打电话。
py: nǐ kě yǐ gěi jīng lǐ fà yóu jiàn huò zhě dǎ diàn huà
en: You can email the manager or call.
why: This is permission stating two possible ways, with no one asked to choose. That is 或者.

q: 头疼的话，你可以吃药___睡一会儿。
zh: 头疼的话，你可以吃药或者睡一会儿。
py: tóu téng de huà nǐ kě yǐ chī yào huò zhě shuì yī huì r
en: If you have a headache, you can take medicine or sleep for a while.
why: The doctor is giving two possible remedies, not asking which. Suggestions listing alternatives use 或者.

q: 下个月我可能去上海___北京出差。
zh: 下个月我可能去上海或者北京出差。
py: xià gè yuè wǒ kě néng qù shàng hǎi huò zhě běi jīng chū chāi
en: Next month I may go to Shanghai or Beijing on a business trip.
why: A statement with 可能 lists two possibilities without asking for a choice, so 或者. 还有 would add a second place, meaning both.

q: 我们可以上午___下午把报告交给经理。
zh: 我们可以上午或者下午把报告交给经理。
py: wǒ men kě yǐ shàng wǔ huò zhě xià wǔ bǎ bào gào jiāo gěi jīng lǐ
en: We can give the report to the manager in the morning or in the afternoon.
why: The sentence says both times are possible; nobody has to decide. Statements use 或者.

q: 如果你不舒服，可以请半天假___回家休息一下。
zh: 如果你不舒服，可以请半天假或者回家休息一下。
py: rú guǒ nǐ bù shū fú kě yǐ qǐng bàn tiān jiǎ huò zhě huí jiā xiū xī yī xià
en: If you don't feel well, you can take half a day off or go home and rest a bit.
why: Two alternative actions are offered as options in a statement, so 或者. 还是 would turn the clause into a question.

q: 她每天下班以后会去跑步___去游泳。
zh: 她每天下班以后会去跑步或者去游泳。
py: tā měi tiān xià bān yǐ hòu huì qù pǎo bù huò zhě qù yóu yǒng
en: After work every day she goes running or swimming.
why: The habit varies between two activities and no question is asked. 或者 lists them. 和 would say she does both every day.

q: 吃完药以后，你可以喝茶___喝水，但是不要喝咖啡。
zh: 吃完药以后，你可以喝茶或者喝水，但是不要喝咖啡。
py: chī wán yào yǐ hòu nǐ kě yǐ hē chá huò zhě hē shuǐ dàn shì bù yào hē kā fēi
en: After taking the medicine you can have tea or water, but not coffee.
why: Both drinks are permitted, so this is a statement listing alternatives: 或者. 还是 would ask the patient to choose.

q: 护士说你可以明天___后天来拿药。
zh: 护士说你可以明天或者后天来拿药。
py: hù shì shuō nǐ kě yǐ míng tiān huò zhě hòu tiān lái ná yào
en: The nurse says you can come for the medicine tomorrow or the day after.
why: The nurse is reporting that either day works, not asking which. A statement that lists options uses 或者.

q: 雨太大了，我们___坐地铁吧。
zh: 雨太大了，我们还是坐地铁吧。
py: yǔ tài dà le wǒ men hái shì zuò dì tiě ba
en: The rain is too heavy; we'd better take the subway.
why: 还是 + verb phrase + 吧 means "had better", after weighing the rain. 或者 and 还有 would add alternatives, not give advice.

q: 你生病了，你___在家休息吧。
zh: 你生病了，你还是在家休息吧。
py: nǐ shēng bìng le nǐ hái shì zài jiā xiū xī ba
en: You're ill; you'd better rest at home.
why: Advice based on a reason (being ill) is 还是 after the subject. 或者 would not fit with 吧.

q: 电梯坏了，我们___走楼梯吧。
zh: 电梯坏了，我们还是走楼梯吧。
py: diàn tī huài le wǒ men hái shì zǒu lóu tī ba
en: The elevator is broken; we'd better take the stairs.
why: Having weighed the situation, the speaker settles on one option: 还是 + 吧 = "had better". 或者 would list another choice.

q: 太晚了，你___明天再去医院吧。
zh: 太晚了，你还是明天再去医院吧。
py: tài wǎn le nǐ hái shì míng tiān zài qù yī yuàn ba
en: It's too late; you'd better go to the hospital tomorrow.
why: The reason clause (too late) forces the "had better" reading with 还是. 或者 cannot give a recommendation with 吧.

q: 我觉得___明天开会好，今天大家都太累了。
zh: 我觉得还是明天开会好，今天大家都太累了。
py: wǒ jué de hái shì míng tiān kāi huì hǎo jīn tiān dà jiā dōu tài lèi le
en: I think it's better to hold the meeting tomorrow; everyone is too tired today.
why: After weighing the options (today versus tomorrow), 还是 marks the preferred one: "better after all". 还有 and 或者 do not express preference.

q: 这个药有点贵，我们___去别的药店看看吧。
zh: 这个药有点贵，我们还是去别的药店看看吧。
py: zhè ge yào yǒu diǎn guì wǒ men hái shì qù bié de yào diàn kàn kàn ba
en: This medicine is a bit expensive; we'd better look at other pharmacies.
why: The price is the reason for changing the plan, which 还是 expresses as a mild suggestion. 或者 would offer a different option instead.

q: 你的感冒还没好，你___别去上班了，在家多休息。
zh: 你的感冒还没好，你还是别去上班了，在家多休息。
py: nǐ de gǎn mào hái méi hǎo nǐ hái shì bié qù shàng bān le zài jiā duō xiū xī
en: Your cold hasn't gotten better; you'd better not go to work and rest more at home.
why: 还是 + 别 is a gentle "had better not" after weighing the cold. 或者 would give an alternative, not advice.

q: 电脑太慢了，我们___换一台新的吧。
zh: 电脑太慢了，我们还是换一台新的吧。
py: diàn nǎo tài màn le wǒ men hái shì huàn yī tái xīn de ba
en: The computer is too slow; we'd better replace it with a new one.
why: After the complaint (too slow) the speaker settles on replacing it: 还是 + verb + 吧. 或者 just lists another possibility.

q: 医生说了很多次，他___不吃药。
zh: 医生说了很多次，他还是不吃药。
py: yī shēng shuō le hěn duō cì tā hái shì bù chī yào
en: The doctor has said it many times, but he still doesn't take the medicine.
why: Nothing changed despite the repeated advice, which is the adverb 还是 "still", placed after the subject. 或者 and 还有 cannot say that.

q: 我吃了药，头___很疼。
zh: 我吃了药，头还是很疼。
py: wǒ chī le yào tóu hái shì hěn téng
en: I took medicine and my head still hurts a lot.
why: The headache has not changed, so the adverb 还是 "still" goes after the subject 头 and before 很疼. 或者 cannot work here.

q: 虽然很忙，他___去看了朋友。
zh: 虽然很忙，他还是去看了朋友。
py: suī rán hěn máng tā hái shì qù kàn le péng yǒu
en: Although he was busy, he still went to see his friend.
why: 虽然 sets up a contrast and 还是 means "all the same". It stands right after the subject 他.

q: 我给他发了三封邮件，他___没回。
zh: 我给他发了三封邮件，他还是没回。
py: wǒ gěi tā fā le sān fēng yóu jiàn tā hái shì méi huí
en: I sent him three emails and he still hasn't replied.
why: Despite three tries the situation is unchanged, which is 还是 "still". 或者 is only a conjunction between options.

q: 已经下班两个小时了，经理___在办公室开会。
zh: 已经下班两个小时了，经理还是在办公室开会。
py: yǐ jīng xià bān liǎng gè xiǎo shí le jīng lǐ hái shì zài bàn gōng shì kāi huì
en: It's been two hours since work ended, and the manager is still in a meeting at the office.
why: Two hours after closing time the situation has not changed, so 还是 "still" fits after the subject 经理. 或者 and 还有 give no such meaning.

q: 他每天都锻炼，可是身体___不太好。
zh: 他每天都锻炼，可是身体还是不太好。
py: tā měi tiān dōu duàn liàn kě shì shēn tǐ hái shì bù tài hǎo
en: He exercises every day, but his health still isn't very good.
why: The result is the same in spite of exercise: 还是 "still" before the adjective phrase. 或者 would need two options to join.

q: ___你来还是不来，我们都要开会。
zh: 不管你来还是不来，我们都要开会。
py: bù guǎn nǐ lái hái shì bù lái wǒ men dōu yào kāi huì
en: Whether you come or not, we are having the meeting.
why: 不管 (or 无论) + A 还是 B + 都 is the frame for "whether A or B". 因为 and 如果 do not combine with 还是 and 都 like this.

q: 不管你去___不去，都告诉我一声。
zh: 不管你去还是不去，都告诉我一声。
py: bù guǎn nǐ qù hái shì bù qù dōu gào su wǒ yī shēng
en: Whether you go or not, let me know.
why: Options after 不管 are joined by 还是. 和 cannot link a verb and its negation, and 吗 would make a question.

q: 不管身体好___不好，每年都应该体检。
zh: 不管身体好还是不好，每年都应该体检。
py: bù guǎn shēn tǐ hǎo hái shì bù hǎo měi nián dōu yīng gāi tǐ jiǎn
en: Whether you are healthy or not, you should have a check-up every year.
why: 不管 asks for two alternatives joined by 还是. 和 would mean "good and not good" and 吗 is not a connector.

q: 不管天气好还是不好，我们___去体检。
zh: 不管天气好还是不好，我们都去体检。
py: bù guǎn tiān qì hǎo hái shì bù hǎo wǒ men dōu qù tǐ jiǎn
en: Whether the weather is good or not, we go for the check-up.
why: The "whatever the case" frame needs 都 after the subject before the verb. 才 means "only then", and 只 means "only".

q: 无论大人还是小孩，医生___会认真检查。
zh: 无论大人还是小孩，医生都会认真检查。
py: wú lùn dà rén hái shì xiǎo hái yī shēng dōu huì rèn zhēn jiǎn chá
en: Whether it is an adult or a child, the doctor examines them carefully.
why: 无论…还是… is closed by 都 in the main clause, saying the result holds in both cases. 才 and 只 give a different meaning.

q: 无论是工作日还是周末，他每天早上___去公园锻炼。
zh: 无论是工作日还是周末，他每天早上都去公园锻炼。
py: wú lùn shì gōng zuò rì hái shì zhōu mò tā měi tiān zǎo shàng dōu qù gōng yuán duàn liàn
en: Whether it's a workday or the weekend, he goes to the park to exercise every morning.
why: The 无论 clause needs 都 after the subject of the main clause. 才 would say he exercises only then, and 只 reads as "only".

q: ___大人还是孩子，都要多喝水。
zh: 无论大人还是孩子，都要多喝水。
py: wú lùn dà rén hái shì hái zi dōu yào duō hē shuǐ
en: Whether adults or children, everyone should drink more water.
why: 无论 + A 还是 B + 都 means "no matter which". 因为 and 虽然 begin different clauses and cannot take 还是 and 都 like this.

zh: 你喝茶还是喝咖啡
py: nǐ hē chá hái shì hē kā fēi
en: Will you have tea or coffee?
why: 还是 sits between the two options in the question. 或者 is not used and no 吗 is added.

zh: 医生问我头疼还是肚子疼
py: yī shēng wèn wǒ tóu téng hái shì dù zi téng
en: The doctor asked me whether I have a headache or a stomachache.
why: The reported question keeps 还是 between the two options. 问 introduces the open choice.

zh: 你还是去医院吧
py: nǐ hái shì qù yī yuàn ba
en: You'd better go to the hospital.
why: 还是 comes before the verb as an adverb of advice, with 吧 at the end of the suggestion.

zh: 我们还是坐出租车去机场吧
py: wǒ men hái shì zuò chū zū chē qù jī chǎng ba
en: We'd better take a taxi to the airport.
why: 还是 stays before the verb phrase and 吧 closes the suggestion; 还是 cannot trail at the end.

zh: 他还是不明白
py: tā hái shì bù míng bái
en: He still doesn't understand.
why: 还是 as "still" stands after the subject and before 不明白. It cannot go before 他 or after 明白.

zh: 虽然很累她还是去上班了
py: suī rán hěn lèi tā hái shì qù shàng bān le
en: Although she was tired, she still went to work.
why: 还是 goes after the subject 她 and before the verb 去. 虽然很累 can be before or after 她.

zh: 不管刮风还是下雨他都去跑步
py: bù guǎn guā fēng hái shì xià yǔ tā dōu qù pǎo bù
en: Whether it's windy or rainy, he goes running.
why: 都 comes after the subject 他 and before 去跑步. It cannot stand in front of 他.

zh: 无论白天还是晚上医院都有医生
py: wú lùn bái tiān hái shì wǎn shàng yī yuàn dōu yǒu yī shēng
en: Whether it is day or night, there are doctors at the hospital.
why: 都 follows the subject 医院 in the main clause. 还是 joins 白天 and 晚上 after 无论.

zh: 周六或者周日都行
py: zhōu liù huò zhě zhōu rì dōu xíng
en: Saturday or Sunday is fine.
why: A statement of acceptable options links them with 或者, and 都 comes before the comment 行.

zh: 我不知道他去还是不去
py: wǒ bù zhī dào tā qù hái shì bù qù
en: I don't know whether he is going or not.
why: 还是 joins the A-not-A choice 去 / 不去 and must sit between them.

task: Ask "rice or noodles?" with 还是 (no 吗).
src_py: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐ fàn ma
zh: 你想吃米饭还是面条
py: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐ fàn hái shì miàn tiáo
en: Do you want to eat rice or noodles?
why: 还是 adds the second option and 吗 is dropped, because the answer is now one of the options, not yes or no.

task: Say "I don't know whether you'll come to work tomorrow or not."
src_py: nǐ míng tiān lái shàng bān ma
zh: 我不知道你明天来上班还是不来
py: wǒ bù zhī dào nǐ míng tiān lái shàng bān hái shì bù lái
en: I don't know whether you're coming to work tomorrow or not.
why: The question becomes the object of 不知道, and the open choice is joined with 还是 between 来上班 and 不来; 吗 disappears.

src: 你可以发邮件，也可以打电话。
task: Combine into one sentence with 或者.
src_py: nǐ kě yǐ fā yóu jiàn yě kě yǐ dǎ diàn huà
zh: 你可以发邮件或者打电话
py: nǐ kě yǐ fā yóu jiàn huò zhě dǎ diàn huà
en: You can send an email or call.
why: Two permitted ways are merged into one statement with 或者, and 可以 is stated only once.

src: 天晴他去上班，下雨他也去上班。
task: Say it with 不管…还是…都.
src_py: tiān qíng tā qù shàng bān xià yǔ tā yě qù shàng bān
zh: 不管天晴还是下雨他都去上班
py: bù guǎn tiān qíng hái shì xià yǔ tā dōu qù shàng bān
en: Whether it's sunny or rainy, he goes to work.
why: 不管 A 还是 B introduces the two conditions and 都 after the subject 他 states that the result is the same.

src: 你来我这儿，或者我去你那儿。
task: Turn it into a choice question with 还是.
src_py: nǐ lái wǒ zhè r huò zhě wǒ qù nǐ nà r
zh: 你来我这儿还是我去你那儿
py: nǐ lái wǒ zhè r hái shì wǒ qù nǐ nà r
en: Will you come to my place, or shall I go to yours?
why: The two options become a question, so 或者 is replaced by 还是 placed before the second clause.

s: 你想喝茶或者咖啡？
s_py: nǐ xiǎng hē chá huò zhě kā fēi
zh: 你想喝茶还是咖啡？
py: nǐ xiǎng hē chá hái shì kā fēi
en: Do you want tea or coffee?
why: Asking the listener to choose needs 还是. 或者 is for statements listing possibilities.

s: 你去开会还是我去开会？
s_py: nǐ qù kāi huì hái shì wǒ qù kāi huì
zh: 你去开会还是我去开会？
py: nǐ qù kāi huì hái shì wǒ qù kāi huì
en: Are you going to the meeting, or shall I go?
why: Two clauses with different subjects can be joined by 还是 in a choice question, and no 吗 is needed.

s: 你想去医院还是在家休息吗？
s_py: nǐ xiǎng qù yī yuàn hái shì zài jiā xiū xī ma
zh: 你想去医院还是在家休息？
py: nǐ xiǎng qù yī yuàn hái shì zài jiā xiū xī
en: Do you want to go to the hospital or rest at home?
why: 还是 already makes this a choice question, so 吗 must go.

s: 你的头是早上疼还是晚上疼吗？
s_py: nǐ de tóu shì zǎo shàng téng hái shì wǎn shàng téng ma
zh: 你的头是早上疼还是晚上疼？
py: nǐ de tóu shì zǎo shàng téng hái shì wǎn shàng téng
en: Does your head hurt in the morning or in the evening?
why: The two options are the answer, so a yes/no particle 吗 cannot be added.

s: 你周六或者周日有空吗？
s_py: nǐ zhōu liù huò zhě zhōu rì yǒu kòng ma
zh: 你周六或者周日有空吗？
py: nǐ zhōu liù huò zhě zhōu rì yǒu kòng ma
en: Are you free on Saturday or Sunday?
why: This is a yes/no question asking whether either day works, so it uses 或者 and 吗 together. 还是 would drop the 吗.

s: 你们先开会还是先吃饭呢？
s_py: nǐ men xiān kāi huì hái shì xiān chī fàn ne
zh: 你们先开会还是先吃饭呢？
py: nǐ men xiān kāi huì hái shì xiān chī fàn ne
en: Shall you have the meeting first or eat first?
why: A choice question may end with the soft particle 呢; only 吗 is excluded.

s: 你打算坐火车去上海还是坐飞机去上海吗？
s_py: nǐ dǎ suàn zuò huǒ chē qù shàng hǎi hái shì zuò fēi jī qù shàng hǎi ma
zh: 你打算坐火车去上海还是坐飞机去上海？
py: nǐ dǎ suàn zuò huǒ chē qù shàng hǎi hái shì zuò fēi jī qù shàng hǎi
en: Are you planning to go to Shanghai by train or by plane?
why: The question asks which means of travel, so no 吗. 还是 already closes the question.

s: 我不知道医生今天在或者不在。
s_py: wǒ bù zhī dào yī shēng jīn tiān zài huò zhě bù zài
zh: 我不知道医生今天在还是不在。
py: wǒ bù zhī dào yī shēng jīn tiān zài hái shì bù zài
en: I don't know whether the doctor is in today or not.
why: After 不知道 the choice is still open, so 还是 joins 在 and 不在. 或者 is not used.

s: 我还没决定去不去开会。
s_py: wǒ hái méi jué dìng qù bù qù kāi huì
zh: 我还没决定去不去开会。
py: wǒ hái méi jué dìng qù bù qù kāi huì
en: I haven't decided whether to go to the meeting.
why: The A-not-A form 去不去 already carries the open choice, so no 还是 is needed.

s: 经理想知道我们明天开会或者后天开会。
s_py: jīng lǐ xiǎng zhī dào wǒ men míng tiān kāi huì huò zhě hòu tiān kāi huì
zh: 经理想知道我们明天开会还是后天开会。
py: jīng lǐ xiǎng zhī dào wǒ men míng tiān kāi huì hái shì hòu tiān kāi huì
en: The manager wants to know whether we will meet tomorrow or the day after.
why: 想知道 introduces an open choice, so 还是 is required. 或者 would claim both are possible.

s: 我下班以后常常看书还是看电影。
s_py: wǒ xià bān yǐ hòu cháng cháng kàn shū hái shì kàn diàn yǐng
zh: 我下班以后常常看书或者看电影。
py: wǒ xià bān yǐ hòu cháng cháng kàn shū huò zhě kàn diàn yǐng
en: After work I often read or watch films.
why: A habit stated as a fact lists alternatives with 或者. 还是 needs a question.

s: 你可以现在去医院，或者明天去。
s_py: nǐ kě yǐ xiàn zài qù yī yuàn huò zhě míng tiān qù
zh: 你可以现在去医院，或者明天去。
py: nǐ kě yǐ xiàn zài qù yī yuàn huò zhě míng tiān qù
en: You can go to the hospital now or go tomorrow.
why: Two permitted options in a statement are linked with 或者, even after a comma.

s: 我们可以周一开会还是周二开会。
s_py: wǒ men kě yǐ zhōu yī kāi huì hái shì zhōu èr kāi huì
zh: 我们可以周一开会或者周二开会。
py: wǒ men kě yǐ zhōu yī kāi huì huò zhě zhōu èr kāi huì
en: We can meet on Monday or Tuesday.
why: This states two possible days, so 或者. 还是 would make an unanswered choice.

s: 外面太冷了，我们在办公室吃还是吧。
s_py: wài miàn tài lěng le wǒ men zài bàn gōng shì chī hái shì ba
zh: 外面太冷了，我们还是在办公室吃吧。
py: wài miàn tài lěng le wǒ men hái shì zài bàn gōng shì chī ba
en: It's too cold outside; we'd better eat in the office.
why: "Had better" 还是 goes after the subject and before the verb phrase, never next to 吧 at the end.

s: 你的感冒还没好，还是在家休息吧。
s_py: nǐ de gǎn mào hái méi hǎo hái shì zài jiā xiū xī ba
zh: 你的感冒还没好，还是在家休息吧。
py: nǐ de gǎn mào hái méi hǎo hái shì zài jiā xiū xī ba
en: Your cold isn't better yet; you'd better rest at home.
why: 还是 can start the clause directly when the subject is clear, with a reason before it. It means "had better", not "or".

s: 他吃了三天药，咳嗽还是没好。
s_py: tā chī le sān tiān yào ké sòu hái shì méi hǎo
zh: 他吃了三天药，咳嗽还是没好。
py: tā chī le sān tiān yào ké sòu hái shì méi hǎo
en: He took medicine for three days and his cough still hasn't gone away.
why: 还是 "still" sits after the subject 咳嗽 and before 没好. The sentence has no choice, so it is not "or".

s: 虽然他很累，他去还是上班了。
s_py: suī rán tā hěn lèi tā qù hái shì shàng bān le
zh: 虽然他很累，他还是去上班了。
py: suī rán tā hěn lèi tā hái shì qù shàng bān le
en: Although he was tired, he still went to work.
why: 还是 "still" must come before the verb 去, directly after the subject. It cannot be placed after 去.

s: 不管天气好还是不好，都我们去体检。
s_py: bù guǎn tiān qì hǎo hái shì bù hǎo dōu wǒ men qù tǐ jiǎn
zh: 不管天气好还是不好，我们都去体检。
py: bù guǎn tiān qì hǎo hái shì bù hǎo wǒ men dōu qù tǐ jiǎn
en: Whether the weather is good or not, we go for the check-up.
why: 都 is an adverb and follows the subject 我们; it cannot come before the subject.

s: 无论是医生还是护士，都要每天洗手。
s_py: wú lùn shì yī shēng hái shì hù shì dōu yào měi tiān xǐ shǒu
zh: 无论是医生还是护士，都要每天洗手。
py: wú lùn shì yī shēng hái shì hù shì dōu yào měi tiān xǐ shǒu
en: Whether doctors or nurses, everyone has to wash their hands every day.
why: 无论 can be followed by 是 and 还是 joins the two nouns; 都 in the main clause is correct.

s: 不管你去和不去，我都会告诉经理。
s_py: bù guǎn nǐ qù hé bù qù wǒ dōu huì gào su jīng lǐ
zh: 不管你去还是不去，我都会告诉经理。
py: bù guǎn nǐ qù hái shì bù qù wǒ dōu huì gào su jīng lǐ
en: Whether you go or not, I will tell the manager.
why: After 不管 the alternatives are joined by 还是. 和 cannot join a verb to its negation.
